openwrt_wiki.factory_header: 128-Byte-Header "device:wnr2200 / version:V1.0.2.24 / region:"; factory-NA mit "region:NA"; letztes Byte Prüfsumme (mkdniimg)
openwrt_wiki.16m_unterschied: The difference between routers sold in Russia and China and other version is flash size. Russian router has MX25L12845EMI-10G which is 16 legged SPI chip with 16M of NOR flash. It is sometimes marketed as WNR2200-100RUS, but router label just says WNR2200.
openwrt_wiki.16m_etikett: Russian (16M) version has three fields with adhesive stickers: SECURITY PIN, SERIAL, MAC; While version sold elsewhere (8M) has four: WiFi Network Name (SSID), Network Key (Password), SERIAL, MAC. ... based on only couple of routers and only definitive ways to determine fw size are via terminal or by looking at the chip itself.
openwrt_wiki.flash_from_openwrt: mtd write: first four bytes of image must be 2200 (32 32 30 30 hex); Stock-Firmware vorher 128-Byte-Header abschneiden
openwrt_wiki.tftp_recovery: Ausschalten, Restore-Factory-Settings-Knopf halten, einschalten, Power-LED blinkt bis dauerhaft grün, dann loslassen; PC 192.168.1.2 an LAN1; tftp put an 192.168.1.1; Flashen 3-7 Minuten
openwrt_wiki.16m_bootloader: There are indications that NMRP protocol can be used to flash it. TFTP recovery method might also work, but can be tricky. Try to watch for power LED, if it starts flashing dimly it is indication, that router is in recovery/upgrade mode.
openwrt_wiki.seriell: on the top, right corner there is already a serial connector. When holding the device with the LAN/Power connectors down, the pinout is like this: <Ground> <RX> <TX> <3,3V> (Hint: You do not need to connect 3,3V when turning the device with the original power supply); the 3,3V pin have a white dot next to it; 115200 8N1, no flow control
openwrt_wiki.uboot_bootlog: U-Boot 1.1.4-gab090933 (Sep 19 2011 - 12:51:47); WNR2200 (ar7241) U-boot dni25 V1.5; DRAM 64 MB (virian ddr1 init); Flash: 8 MB; TFTP Server Firmware Recovery mode an 192.168.1.1:69
openwrt_wiki.kernel_bootlog: SoC Atheros AR7241 rev 1; MIPS 24Kc; CPU 360 MHz, DDR 360 MHz, AHB 180 MHz; mx25l6405d (8192 Kbytes); mtdparts u-boot 256k, u-boot-env 64k, firmware 7808k, art 64k; eth0 MII (PHY), eth1 GMII built-in switch; AR9287 Rev:2; EHCI 1 Port
openwrt_wiki.gpio_ar7241: LED: LAN2 amber 0, LAN4 amber 1, LAN1 amber 6, WPS grün 7, USB grün 8, LAN3 amber 11, WAN amber 12, LAN1-4 grün 13-16, WAN grün 17 (alle active low)
openwrt_wiki.gpio_ar9287: WLAN blau 53, Power amber 54, Power grün 55, RFKILL-Taste 56, USB +5V 57 (active high), WPS-Taste 58, RESET-Taste 59
openwrt_wiki.trivia: Stock-Firmware ist altes OpenWrt Kamikaze 7.09 (BusyBox 1.4.2), Telnet per telnetenable, Gearguy:Geardog
